LESSON: WRITING 4.4.1 HANDWRITING / BRAILLE WRITING

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.4: Writing 4.4.1 Handwriting / Braille writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 4.4.1 Handwriting / Braille writing, part of Strand 4 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How do we write clearly and neatly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 4.4.1 Handwriting / Braille writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Digital literacy- The learner's ability to use digital devices with assistive technology is enhanced as they use the internet to connect and watch or listen

to videos on formation of target letters and practise forming the letters.

Values:
Unity is enhanced as the learner displays team spirit as they work together.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills (self-esteem): The learner enhances levels of self-esteem as they use neat and legible handwriting in writing

Links to other Learning Areas:
The learner uses correct letter formation as they write materials in other learning areas.

Suggested learning resources

• Braille letter cards,

• Audio video clip,

• Textbooks in braille and in appropriate font and colour contrast,

Suggested vocabulary
